identity.realm: Fourteenth gate, and the heel vessels are why. A marshfolk wades on a three-point stance distributed over splayed toes and a tail-prop, so a heel never takes a full load and qi never pools there. The fourteenth is the first gate that needs both heel vessels pressurised at once, so it is not a wall she is walking toward: it is a gate her construction never built the plumbing for. She holds the eleventh comfortably. The upper three are decoration in her body.

appearance.presentation: Sedge Ambal stands in the water rather than on it, always, with the weight settled across two points and the tail-prop taking the third behind her.
appearance.age: Thirty-four, which for her line is the age at which the rafts stop being somebody else's problem and start being hers.
appearance.build: Marshfolk, a wading amphibian lineage native to the floodplain margin. Splayed three-point feet, a prehensile tail-prop she leans on, feathered inlet and outlet, and a ventral brood pouch. There is no heel, and no structure standing in for one. Long-legged and low through the hips, the pelvic basin broad and shallow. She is buoyant rather than heavy and gets heavier every gate, which is the whole of what the discipline does to her.
appearance.complexion: Grey-green and permanently damp at the cuffs. Her skin dries fast out of the water and cracks at the ankle, and she has never once been able to explain that to a dry-land physician.
appearance.hair: Coarse, black, kept in a single heavy rope she re-wraps wet. It has never once been cut short and she resents anyone who suggests it.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and dark-adapted to a low horizon. She finds a lit room uncomfortable in a way she describes as tiredness.
appearance.palette: Silt brown, wet slate, reed green, and a bone-white that only appears where the water has left her own salt behind.
appearance.attire: Layered oilskin over a felted reed underlayer, high collar, sleeves to the wrist, boots made for a foot that is not a foot. The mat is lashed across her back in every scene that is not the sitting.
appearance.marks: A pale band at each ankle where the stance has been loading the wrong joints for thirty years, and eleven small cuts in the left forearm from reed work that never once healed cleanly.
appearance.bearing: Low, unhurried, and slightly out of balance to anyone not raised on silt. She leans on things and does not seem to notice.

canon.role_in_story: Every cultivation discipline in this setting is a daily sitting at a fixed hour in a fixed place, and Sedge Ambal is the one body on the pass for whom none of those three things can be true. Her qi is quick in wet qi and markedly slow on dry land, so the hour her practice is worth doing is the hour the marsh is under water, and the marsh is under water on a schedule set by a river basin two hundred miles away that has never once consulted her. She sits anyway, on a woven reed mat she carries rolled across her back, because the mat is her species' only maternity provision and it is furniture only while there is standing water beneath it. The pass polity she books her seasons against sets its calendar by the Tidemark, so the year she lives in is owned by a tide and the year she practises in is owned by a river, and no office in this setting can hold a date for either of them.
canon.first_appearance: First seen wading the Bitter Scrub margin at the grey hour before the shift, sitting on her mat in standing water with the count kept in her head and no sheet of paper anywhere near her, while the pass clerk's season-book lay open on a desk two hundred miles away.
canon.lore: A marshfolk's eggs are laid in a mat of woven reed, carried under the brood pouch through the dry season and hatched when the water returns, and that fact organises the whole of this species' life more thoroughly than any office ever has. An office that is dry for four months of the year has no row on any roll the plains keep, which is why Sedge Ambal has held a pass posting for eleven years and appears on no register that anybody can produce. She is the ford-keeper's relief on the marsh crossing, and the crossing is a marsh crossing, which means her post is legible to anybody who wades it and invisible to anybody who reads. She is good at the work in a way that is difficult to overstate: she reads current and silt at a glance, she knows where the holding ground is under a hundredweight sack before she is asked, and she has twice refused a party she would not cross and been right both times about why. What she cannot do is arrive at the same hour twice in a season. Her qi pools low and wide in that broad pelvic basin rather than in a compact chest seat, so she takes charge out of wet ground efficiently and out of dry ground so poorly that a sitting held on the crust is close to a waste of her afternoon. The discipline she was given is a discipline of stillness, and it is not that she cannot be still. It is that stillness only pays her in one place, and that place is a marsh, and the marsh is a calendar she does not hold. She has opened the eleventh gate, which is the last one that asks anything of a stance that never loads a heel. Above it the fourteenth wants both heel vessels pressurised at the same instant, and there is no version of that in a body whose heel has never once carried a full load. She has been offered the higher rungs twice by people who assumed the arithmetic was the obstacle and were not listening when she gave it to them. What she wants is narrower than a rung. She wants a date. The pass clerk's season-book is the only record in this setting that would let a person book a practice against a flood, and it is written in a hand that is not hers and kept at a desk that is dry all year, and she has never once been asked what she would enter in it. She keeps her own count instead, in her head, in the way her line has kept counts since the water changed and nobody came. That count is the only evidence in this setting that her species has ever exercised a path at all, and it dies with her, which she knows, and has never once written down.
history: Was hatched from a mat in the third year of the run's move and carried the dry season under her mother's pouch, which is the ordinary marshfolk childhood and the reason no roll in this setting has ever held her.

Began the daily sitting at eleven because the only teacher available was a mind-path practitioner who insisted the mind path did not care, and was right: the wet ground carried her, not the instruction.
Was given a pass term by a clerk who wanted a body at the crossing and did not want the paperwork of hiring one, and has held it for eleven years unrecorded, which suits her and suits the clerk.
Refused two offers of the higher rungs from people who treated the twenty-fourth-ordinal arithmetic as the whole difficulty, and has stopped explaining the heel.
Learned in her twentieth year that her count would die with her, and declined the one invitation to write it down that has ever been made to her.

personality.summary: A marshfolk qi practitioner whose discipline is worth nothing to her on dry ground and whose every date belongs to a river. She is the most reliable body at a marsh crossing and the only person on the pass with no register at all.
traits: Counts continuously, in her head, and has never once been asked to produce the count.
Reads current and silt before she has finished crossing them.
Refuses work she cannot vouch for and explains the refusal in one sentence.
Unbothered by being unrecorded and genuinely unwilling to be recorded.
Keeps a mat lashed to her back at all times, including indoors, including in houses with floors.
mannerisms: Leans on whatever is within reach, and does not register that she is doing it.
Crouches rather than bends, because crouching does not load a heel.
Answers a question about a date by asking what the water is doing.
Sits when she is listening, which she was taught and never unlearned.
motivations: To be given a date she can plan a sitting around.
To have her count held somewhere that outlives her.
To be the reason nobody drowns at that crossing.
flaws: Will not enter anything, which costs her standing she cannot spend.
Assumes her own method generalises, and has never tested it anywhere with less water under it.
Cannot be made urgent. She has been slow to raise an alarm twice and wrong both times about the reason.
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried, and mostly interrogative. She states a conclusion as a question she expects the ground to answer, and she does not raise her voice, because a voice carries badly over water and she has never had a room to raise it in.
taboos: Sitting on dry ground on purpose.
Signing a register that would make the count citable and therefore contestable.
Taking a crossing fee for a party she has not read herself.

relationships.note: The only ground on which her practice is worth the hour it costs, and the ground whose regrowth rate sets her season without asking.

A people who measure a life by how many gates were already shut when its holder was born; hers arrived with every path open, a third of a parent's lifespan and no way to spend a century getting ready.

The densest body in the record stops at seventeen because its density will not let a cavity form. She stops at fourteen because a heel has never carried a load. Both are anatomy arguing with a gate, and neither of them chose it.

Longwinter qi accumulates rather than circulates and a breakthrough arrives when the reserve is full; hers is quick in wet qi and slow on dry, so the same gate waits on a river instead of on a season.
The registry reads the dead as the frame said and keeps the burnt list. It has no row for a woman who has never been on it and whose species was never on it either.

The folded bedding under a frame that writes all six law groups is the deepest karst on the plains, and neither a marshfolk nor her parent can leave a cave system. She is nine gates below a wall she could name, and cannot reach a mountain to look at it.

reference_stats.summary: She refines faster out of wet ground than anything else on the pass and slower on dry than a commonborn, and the discipline that would make her formidable is a discipline of sitting in one place. She cannot be hurried, cannot be posted to anything above the marsh line, and is at her best exactly where the water is.
strengths: Takes charge out of standing water efficiently and out of dry ground barely at all, so a sitting at the right hour is worth several at the wrong one.
Holds the eleven ordinary vessels and the four reservoirs without effort, because none of those asks a stance to load a heel.
Reads current, silt depth and holding ground at a distance, which makes her the only body at a marsh crossing that cannot be walked into by surprise.
Her frame broadens and densifies evenly rather than at a point, so a blade finds no purchase and every gate she passes makes her heavier without making her slower.
weaknesses: A dry sitting is close to a wasted hour, and the pass has four months a year when every hour is dry.
The three-point stance is why the fourteenth gate exists as a wall and no amount of practice changes it.
No advance more than a few paces per gate, and she cannot be posted to ground that is not a marsh.
The reflex to crouch and lean makes her read as unsteady to any authority that assesses bodies by how they stand.
reference_stats.combat_read: Unassailable in water and negligible on a dry floor, which is a map problem rather than a fighting one. She will not be pressured into a standing fight and has lost the only two she entered, both on ground she chose badly and both because she spent the first minutes crouched. Fought on her own terms, in the shallows, she is close to unkillable by anything that works through a meridian, and helpless against anything that waits for the tide to go out.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is anatomical and institutional rather than mechanical, and the bible does not state it as a rule, so it is authored rather than quoted. Her advantage is wet ground. Her cost is that the practice which exploits it is a discipline of remaining still in one place, and the one place is a marsh whose schedule is a river's. No cultivation technique, item or realm changes the heel, and nothing in the setting gives a body a heel it did not grow. The three-second version: she is the fastest qi body at a river crossing and there is no ladder on the bank.

art.palette_notes: Reed, wet slate and silt. The palette is the marsh's own and the only saturated note in her is the bone-white her own salt leaves on the oilskin.

identity.realm: Ordinal four, and the fourth gate is the yin organs, inherited from the mineral parent without alteration because heat is not a second organ. He has a working fire circulation in a mineral lattice and no paired organ set to run a channel between, so there is nothing above the fourth for him to build into. He is the most durable body anyone can build, the fastest qi throughput of any durable body, and it has bought him a quarter of the ladder on a span of about sixty years. Both facts are the same fact, and he has stopped needing them to be two.

appearance.presentation: Rennick Vask stands like something that was placed rather than grew, and puts one hand on worked stone whenever there is any within reach.
appearance.age: Fifty-one, on a sixty-year span, which makes every plan he makes a nine-year plan and he has made a great many of them.
appearance.build: Stonebound, the one documented crossing of the mineral body with the fire body, kept and named as a line rather than noted as an oddity. A mineral lattice with a working fire circulation inside it and sixty years of life. The densest frame anybody can build and the only one here with no dantian. Broad through the chest and low at the centre of gravity, and warmer to the touch than the air he is standing in.
appearance.complexion: A mineral grey under a permanent bloom of fine ash, with a seam at the collarbone where the fire shows through as heat rather than colour.
appearance.hair: Cropped hard and grey at the temples twenty years early, which on this body is a thermal fact and not a year of worry.
appearance.eyes: Pale and steady, and the only part of him that looks like a person at a glance rather than a wall.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, iron black, and a low ember orange that only shows at the lattice seam and in the eyes when the day is nearly done.
appearance.attire: Boiled leather over the shoulders, high collar, sleeves fastened at the wrist against the heat. Furnace-side of the guild kit, and he has never once been able to take it off without his frame cooling faster than the day allows.
appearance.marks: A lattice of hairline seam-scars across the right forearm, where the frame has split and re-fused along the fire circulation and never quite matched itself twice.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still unless he is working, and then unhurried in a way that looks like slowness until you see what he is reading.

canon.role_in_story: A stonebound's qi path is the fastest of any durable body in this setting and it terminates at the fourth gate, and Rennick Vask's whole life has been organised around the fact that nobody in the world is able to check either of those statements. The Sixth Reading is the only instrument that holds a law apart from its effect, and its own record says it cannot be performed on this body by a practitioner or an observer, because a frame crowded enough to hold a law apart needs a paired organ set and he has one cavity with a fire circulation in it. So he refines faster than anything mortal and there is no reading in this setting that can say so. The only religion that would take a measurement off him opens bodies at burial, on the doctrine that a body is fuel and the dead are fuel not yet spent, and it has no rite at all for a frame that was unsealed once by evolution and has never stopped burning.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the toe of the ashfall belt with one palm flat on a cut face, reading the seam work off the stone and being told by the shift foreman that nothing could be certified from him either way.
canon.lore: The Ember Cradle made exactly one crossing between a burning body and a mineral one at a founding generation and has never repeated it, because a second crossing averages the concentration out. That single instance is the reason the Emberborn line is recorded alongside the stone line at all, and the crossing survives as a household memory rather than as a technique, which means this body cannot be taught by anybody who was not in that generation and cannot be reproduced by anybody at all. Rennick Vask is the last of it. The mineral half does not regenerate and the fire half cannot be extinguished, so he heals nothing and cools nothing, and the two facts together are the most durable frame in this setting on a span of about sixty years, which makes him worth enormously more to an employer than a commonborn is and means his guild's own arrangement with him is unrenewable in a way no roster admits. His qi is the fastest through any durable body in the record: the fire parent donates the throughput and nothing else, and a mineral frame conducts the heat away so efficiently that the charge arrives and departs before any gate can hold it. The first three gates come and go quickly and he has never once had to work for one. The fourth is the yin organs, which want four distinct structures with a channel running between each pair, and he has one cavity. That is the wall. Above it there is nothing in this setting for him, and above him there is nothing either: a denser frame cannot be written into a second layer at all, so his species stops exactly where the world becomes layered. What he has instead is speed with no ceiling, which is a rate and not a magnitude, and every authority in this setting has spent his working life confusing the two. Nobody can read him. The one instrument that can hold a law apart from its effect requires a frame with room to spare, and the doctrine of the school that treats the law table as a closed budget cannot file a body whose capability exceeds what any register can see of it. He has therefore spent thirty years as the only body on the belt whose gains are real, fast and entirely unattested, and he has spent them being useful, because being useful is the only standing a frame with no certificate can hold. The religion that would settle it opens bodies at burial and recovers what is in them, and he has been to its court once, to be looked at, and was told plainly that there is nothing here to recover. He has never forgotten the courtesy of it.
history: Was shaped into the line at a founding generation and is the last body carrying that specific crossing, which makes him a document rather than a population.
Cleared the first three qi gates before he was seventeen, faster than anything on the belt, and learned early that nobody would ever be able to confirm it.
Took a furnace-side guild term on a cold road because the house could not otherwise staff a guarantor, and discovered the term outlasts the house's interest in him by a decade.
Was carried to the Unsealed Court to be opened for measurement and told there was nothing to recover, and has worked since out of an entirely private discipline that no rite covers.

Refused an offer of a mineral frame cut fresh from the bed, on the arithmetic that the resource the setting ran out of is the only thing that could have extended this body and cannot be had at any price.

personality.summary: The fastest qi in any durable body and the only frame in this setting that cannot be read while it works. He is the standing proof that the density ceiling is a material fact, and the one person nobody can cite.
traits: Reads worked stone by laying on it, and reads it better than any instrument on the ridge.
Conceals nothing and offers nothing, and is read as calm by people who have not noticed they are getting no more than he means to give.
Plans in nine-year horizons because he has to, and does not resent it so much as he used to.
Will not take a frame he cannot pay for, at any price, including his own life.
Keeps a discipline nobody taught him and cannot publish, because publishing it would be a reading he cannot permit.
mannerisms: Puts one hand on any worked surface within reach.
Stops entirely still at the moment of a gate, which reads as inattention to anybody not looking for it.
Cannot be seated comfortably in furniture built for a lighter body and has stopped apologising for it.
Answers a question about his limits with a number, and the number is always the same number.
motivations: To be measured once, by somebody with no standing to lose, before the sixty years are gone.
To be useful enough that the question never has to be asked again.
To keep the crossing from being averaged away by being retried.
flaws: Refuses every offer of help on the grounds that help implies a debt, and is therefore alone at exactly the wrong rate.
Cannot distinguish an important reading from a comfortable one, because no one has ever given him either.
Treats his own sixty years as a fixed term and spends them like one, which reads as calm and is mostly arithmetic.
personality.voice: Low, slow and extremely literal. He gives figures rather than impressions and will repeat one if pressed. He has been known to describe what his frame is doing with the vocabulary of a man describing a furnace, because that is the vocabulary he was given.
taboos: Being opened, looked inside, or certified.
A second crossing of the two lines, in any direction, by anybody.
Signing anything that would let a frame be cut for him.

relationships.note: The mineral parent donates the frame and the ceiling. Ordinal four, inherited unchanged, because heat is not a second organ. His line is that body bred back toward flesh and is more alive and less capable for it.
The fire parent donates the throughput and nothing else. The density doubles the fire parent's lifespan and the lifespan is still the reason this body is a problem.

Holding a law apart from its effect needs a frame crowded enough to have room to spare. He has a working circulation and no paired organ set, so the reading cannot be performed on him by a practitioner or an observer.

The dead are unsealed at burial and their core resumes work in the frame, so a body is fuel and the dead are fuel not yet spent. This species was unsealed once by evolution and has never stopped burning, which the theology has no rite for.
No socket may be opened once sealed, and reforging is the one act the temple's own forge may not perform. He has been opened once, politely, and there was nothing inside worth taking.

Iron ore is the mortal tier's only dense material and the only thing a core can be caged in, and he carried his own cage, so the resource the setting ran out of is the only thing that could have extended him and cannot be had at any price.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest durable qi in the record, terminating at the fourth gate because heat is not a second organ, and entirely uncertifiable because the only instrument that could take his reading requires the paired organs he does not have.
strengths: Refines faster than any other durable body, so the first three gates cost him almost nothing and the early part of any practice is free.
Cannot be put down by anything that works through a meridian, and recovers nothing, so a fight cannot wait him out.
Reads a worked surface by laying on it and gets a figure off rock that no instrument on the ridge will return.
Durable under load for two lifetimes of a commonborn, which makes him the most valuable body on a spoil heap and the least replaceable.
weaknesses: The fourth gate is a wall, not a height: one cavity and no paired organ set, so there is no channel to run between anything.
Nothing in this setting can take his reading, so his gains are real and have never once been provable to anybody but him.
Heals nothing and cools nothing, so a fifty-year-old frame and a fifty-one-year-old frame are not the same object.
His qi arrives and departs so fast that a gate cannot hold it, which means his rate is enormous and his reserve is nil.
reference_stats.combat_read: A body that fights for about thirty seconds before anything structural arrives, and then does not stop for a very long time. Nothing delivered through a meridian lands. Nothing delivered by weight either, over long enough — he does not tire, because there is nothing in him being repaired and nothing in him being spent. What ends a fight with him is attrition of a different kind: taking the ground out from under the work, or simply outlasting the ninety seconds it takes a fire body of his kind to run out of margin. He knows that and prices his own work accordingly, which is why he has never once been in a fight he did not choose the ground for.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is anatomical and institutional rather than mechanical. His advantage is that the mineral frame conducts the fire parent's heat away, which is what makes him the fastest qi body on the plains. His cost is that the same conduction means nothing above the fourth gate can hold a charge long enough to become a cavity, and that the only instrument built to settle the question needs the paired organ set his frame never grew. The bible states the sixth reading's inapplicability to this body directly; it does not state a rule that his rate and his ceiling are the same fact, and that reading is mine. Short version: nobody can prove he is any good, and he is.

identity.realm: No ladder at all, and this is the species' fact rather than hers. All three of a saltwrack's paths are complete and none has ever been exercised at any scale, because the basin brine was replaced rather than drained and three generations of famine took the rest. The wall every saltfolk meets at the eleventh, where the brine sac splits the penetrating vessel, is decorative in her line because nobody in it ever got near it. She has opened two ordinary gates herself and holds the only record that her species has ever touched a path at all, and it is in her head.

appearance.presentation: Ilbre Sorrel stands on the crust with her weight even and her tongue slightly out, reading the wind, and sits to do anything that takes concentration.
appearance.age: Twenty-six, in the last generation that is viable, which on a clade whose fertility was failing on schedule is the most contested year of her life.
appearance.build: Saltwrack, a saltfolk clade stranded on an evaporite basin whose brine was wholly replaced. A saltfolk body, slightly more gracile, with a shallower brine sac, and a taste that reads the new brine perfectly well. Gracile for a saltfolk and thin across the shoulders, with the shallower sac that came with the narrowing. The body reads as under-built and is not, which is the gracility every specimen shares and a real population difference rather than an artefact.
appearance.complexion: Pale and faintly crystalline at the knuckles, drying out above the brine line faster than a body of any other species in this setting.
appearance.hair: Bleached to nothing at the ends and kept in a working braid, because there is no water on this basin worth wetting it in.
appearance.eyes: Narrow and salt-crusted at the corners. She reads a surface by tasting it and can tell four orders of dilution apart, which nobody involved found useful at the time.
appearance.palette: Bone, pale brine-green, and a white crust at every hem, with the one dark note in her at the throat where the sac sits.
appearance.attire: Layered against a dry wind, high collar, sleeves closed, a wide belt with a stoppered flask on it that is almost never empty and is never full.
appearance.marks: A salt bloom across the forearms that has stopped spreading, and a split nail on the left hand from a sealed cap she has opened more times than she will admit.
appearance.bearing: Careful, unhurried and conserving, the walk of somebody who cannot afford to be wrong about a surface.

canon.role_in_story: The Saltwrack were stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than drained, so everything they were built to drink became poison to them and everything they could tolerate became nutritionally empty, and they were never hunted. Ilbre Sorrel is the last generation that is still viable, and she is viable because one sealed sump on a basin that no longer produces any still holds the previous chemistry. She has worked out that the discipline of refinement is a daily accumulation, and that the only supply she has is the same closed volume of water that keeps her body alive, and that a sitting therefore is a withdrawal from her own life. The house that might otherwise have held the figure is forbidden by its own founding rule to write it down.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the sealed cap with both hands on it, counting the volume before she drank, in front of two dry-salt company men who had come to price the basin and found the only person on it unwilling to be a free survey.
canon.lore: The basin was certified three times with three answers that nobody compared, and the substitution that killed this clade would have been one assay away from being caught three generations early. The replacement water is potable and is poison to her. The replacement crust is food and is nutritionally empty. Her taste reads the new brine perfectly well and could have said so at any point in three generations, and the detail nobody involved found useful at the time was exactly this one: that the survivors could taste what had happened to them. What nobody established is whether the taste was ever exercised as an instrument, and the answer is no, because a body that can read four orders of dilution and has no market for the reading is not an instrument. It is a person. She is the second person, and the first was her grandmother, who mentioned it once to a house surveyor and was not believed because the surveyor had a figure of her own. So the line kept drinking and kept counting and told nobody, which is the ledger's own failure rather than its secrecy: the house that keeps its real figures in the head of one member not permitted to write them down was founded to keep figures out of a counting house, and it has held that rule faithfully through a famine it could have named. What she cultivates with is the sump. Not drinking from it — drinking from it is ordinary and is how the line stays alive — but sitting on it, daily, running the refinement discipline against a fixed volume of the only water her body can metabolise, and watching the margin go down by a measurable amount each time. She has opened two ordinary gates that way. That is the entire cultivation history of her species and she is the only living person who can produce it, and it is kept in her head because the arrangement that would otherwise hold the figure in a head forbids writing it down. She has considered breaking the rule. She has not, and the reason is not obedience: it is that a number somebody else can read is a number somebody else can dispute, and she is the only person alive who knows what the water tastes like, and a dispute about her water is a dispute she would lose on standing rather than on fact. The flood that recharged the sump on a schedule nobody decided is not coming back, and the sump has a finite volume, and she is spending it at a rate she can state exactly, which is a thing almost nobody in this setting can say about anything.
history: Was carried through her first dry season as an infant on the sealed sump's margin, which is the only reason she is alive and the reason nobody expected a viable generation.
Learned the taste from her grandmother at about six, and learned in the same conversation that it was not to be mentioned to surveyors.
Opened her first ordinary gate at nineteen by sitting on the sump, and worked out within a year that every sitting was a withdrawal.
Told a house surveyor what the water tasted like, once, at eleven, and was not believed because he had a figure of his own and she had none.
Counted the sump's decline for six years without writing any of it down, and decided against breaking the house rule on the ground that a disputable number would be lost to her on standing.

personality.summary: A saltwrack qi practitioner in the last viable generation of a clade that was never hunted and never counted. She cultivates against a fixed volume of the only water she can drink, so her practice is a withdrawal from her own life, and she is the sole holder of the only record her species has.
traits: Tastes a surface before she will stand on it and can tell four orders of dilution apart.
Keeps an exact volume count in her head and has never written a figure down in her life.
Refuses to be a free survey and has said so to a company man to his face.
Economical in everything, including speech, because her line learned economy in a famine.
Unbroken by the loss of the line, which she has decided in advance is the only attitude that lets her keep working.
mannerisms: Sits for anything requiring concentration, and sits with her back to a wall by reflex.
Wets the corner of her lip before she answers a question she does not like.
Counts in her head visibly, and stops the moment anybody notices.
Checks the flask before she sits down anywhere, which is a habit and not a vice.
motivations: To reach the point where the figure can be written down by somebody with more standing than she has.
To be wrong about the basin by a measurable amount, for once.
To have her grandmother's reading confirmed by something other than her own mouth.
flaws: Will not break the house rule, and the rule is the reason nobody can help her.
Believes she is the last, and has stopped building anything that outlives the sump.
Cannot separate her judgement from her family's, and knows it, and proceeds anyway.
personality.voice: Quiet, clipped and entirely concrete. She talks in volumes and tastes and dates, and when she is uncertain she says what she tasted rather than what she thinks, which in her family is the same sentence.
taboos: Writing the figure down in any form.
Drinking from a supply she has not read herself.
Accepting a price named first by a buyer, which her basin never managed once and she will not manage now.

relationships.note: One evaporite basin, wholly replaced, and there has never been any other. The replacement water is potable and is poison to her; the replacement crust is food and is nutritionally empty.

The dominion's territory is exactly its waterline, and this is the part of that territory the waterline crossed. The dominion's own definition of itself is what did the killing and it has never been asked about it.

The house's real figures live in the head of one member who is not permitted to write them down, and the one figure that would have saved this clade was the basin's chemistry. It was held by nobody's head, because there was no house left to hold it in.

Disagreement between surveys is what makes a certification necessary, and this basin's chemistry was certified three times with three answers nobody compared. The question that matters after a substitution is when it was first measurable.

The one plant authored into all four tiers at once is the control the new brine failed. The replacement crust was food and it was nutritionally empty, which is the only measurement in the record that distinguishes a famine from a substitution.
A saltfolk concentrates salt past the point ordinary water poisons and cannot leave the pan. She is a gracile version of that body on a pan where the thing it was built to drink is gone.

reference_stats.summary: She refines against a fixed, finite volume of the only water her body can metabolise, so every sitting costs her margin, and the species' whole cultivation history is two gates held in the head of one person who is forbidden to write them down.
strengths: Tastes four orders of dilution apart, so she can date a substitution from a sample that any other instrument in this setting would call water.
The only living reader of the chemistry that killed her clade, which makes her a control case that cannot be re-run.
Refines efficiently out of brine that would poison a body of any other species, so her supply is a substance nothing else can use.
Economical to a degree that reads as calm, because a famine teaches economy and her line was given three generations of it.
weaknesses: Every sitting is a withdrawal from a closed volume, so her practice has a cost that increases every time she uses it.
The body is gracile and the sac shallow, so she has almost no margin above the brine line and no reserve at all above the sump.
She dies on fresh ground, and there is a great deal of fresh ground.
Her only evidence cannot be written down, so nothing she knows can be used by anyone without her word.
reference_stats.combat_read: Essentially a non-combatant and knows it. She has two ordinary gates and no frame worth the name, and anything that reaches her across dry ground is a problem she has no answer to. What she can do is refuse, delay and know, and the third is the one that matters: she can date a substitution in front of a buyer, out loud, from a taste, and a man who needs the basin priced correctly has a strong incentive to keep her alive and a very weak one to believe her.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is anatomical and it is the reason her discipline has a price. A saltfolk's advantage is that it can metabolise brine no softer body could drink, which means her supply is a substrate nothing else in the setting can use, and it also means the substrate is the whole of what keeps her alive. Cultivation is accumulation and the volume is closed, so cultivation and survival are the same arithmetic. The bible states the total dependence and the sealed sump and the three generations of famine; it does not state that a daily sitting draws on the lifeline, and that connection is mine rather than quoted. Nothing here is a mechanical rule I invented — no technique, item or realm changes it, because the volume is a volume.

name: Thessa Kall
aliases: the control that will not sit still

identity.realm: No ladder at all, and the absence is structural rather than modest. A mineral bloom holds qi where a fungal colony transacted with it, so nothing in her body is constrained by a structure she does not have: there is no ceiling to quote because there is no gate to fail. Her species' own record says its ceiling is unbounded. What she cannot do is say where she is on anything, because a subspecies that has never had rungs has never had a rung to name, and the discipline she practises is spent on a ladder that does not price it.

appearance.presentation: Thessa Kall stands very still and turns her head last, because she can see in the dark and there is no reason to move like somebody who cannot.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight, on a ninety-year life, which is a third of what her parent species gets and the arithmetic of that is the whole shape of her career.
appearance.build: Deadlight, a lanternfolk subspecies whose fungal colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom. A lanternfolk body with a silicate lattice where the hyphal colony was — lighter, colder, entirely inert, and grown around rather than recovered. Lanternfolk frame with a lattice instead of a colony. Lighter than her parents by a considerable margin and oddly buoyant, and nothing in it is being repaired.
appearance.complexion: Cool to the touch and slightly translucent at the thin places, with a faint mineral sheen at the collarbone that catches a lamp and gives none back.
appearance.hair: Fine, colourless, grown slowly and cut with a blade rather than a shear because it does not respond to one.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary human eyes that see in this dark without any help, which is the single most-cited difference between her line and her parents' and the reason both are named for it.
appearance.palette: Pale mineral grey, cold blue-white at the lattice, and the warm lamp-glow of everybody else on the quarry floor, which is the only warm thing in her pictures and is not hers.
appearance.attire: Quarry issue over a high collar, sleeves closed to the wrist, a lamp on a hook that she does not need and carries for other people.
appearance.marks: A pale, hard bloom at the base of the throat where the lattice replaced the colony, and a white streak on one knuckle from a cut that closed in a mineral crust instead of scar tissue.
appearance.bearing: Patient and slightly too still, and reads to strangers as someone who has stopped listening rather than someone who can hear.

canon.role_in_story: Her species is the control case: a cave people who outsourced their nervous system to a luminous fungal colony, and a lineage whose colony strain failed and was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom that could survive the same conditions. Losing the colony cost two hundred and fifty years of life and gave back the mind path, and the subspecies is the whole of one side of that dispute recorded on a body where both effects can be measured against the parent. Thessa Kall cultivates qi in a frame that has no ceiling because it has no structure to be constrained by, and the discipline is not readable from her because there is no ladder that prices it. What makes it a pressure rather than a triumph is the lichen: a mineral bloom is precisely the substrate the trial-field lichen colonises, wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through worked stone. So every gate she opens writes a permanent marker on the quarry wall, and the survey culture she works inside will not accept a reading until a second person has heard it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a face cut the previous day on the quarry floor, standing in the dark with the lamp off, waiting for a second reader who had not arrived, and perfectly content to wait.
canon.lore: A deadlight's bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, and that is the entire difference from a colony: nothing that enters her is spent and nothing in her is repaired. She cannot be tired in the ordinary way and she cannot be healed in the ordinary way, and on a ninety-year span that is not a detail. It is the reason she has forty years of practice in her and no prospect of the century that a body's honest education requires. She has an unmediated interior, which is what a lost symbiosis gives back along with the mind path, and that interior is the reason she can tell anybody anything at all about what a qi practice feels like from the inside — and also the reason there is nobody in this setting with standing to check her. She is the only body in the record where the colony did for its parent and the colony prevented are both readable on one frame, and she carries that without being asked to. What she has built around that fact is a practice, and the practice has a consequence she did not anticipate and cannot undo. The trial-field lichen colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it. A mineral bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, which is exactly the substrate the marker grows on, and exactly the difference her subspecies is named for. So every gate she opens leaves a growth on the quarry wall, in the ordinary way, where a working face cuts fresh rock every day. She is the only body in this setting whose practice is published in somebody else's ledger without her having written a word. The survey culture she works for holds that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it, and the one body on the plains that can also hear is her. She can give the reading. What she cannot do is be cross-examined about it, because a lichen does not answer and the thing she is describing on that wall is her own interior. Every marker is a fact about her, made by her own work, visible to anyone with a lamp, and about her own qi rather than about the stone. She has tried twice to have a marker read as a mineral reading and has been refused twice, correctly, because it is not one. There is no column anywhere in the setting for a practice that records itself in the ground, and there is no office that wants one, because an office wants a person to be sitting on a rung and she is not sitting on anything.
history: Was born in the last cavern generation of a colony line, on the far side of a strain failure nobody diagnosed in time.
Was the first of her line to see in the dark, which was treated as a curiosity and then as a useful night trade.
Took a quarry term at about thirty because a body that sees in the dark is worth a great deal at a face that has not been cut yet.
Found the first lichen marker on her own cut at about forty and spent three years establishing that it was hers and could not be anybody else's.
Attempted twice to have a marker entered as a mineral reading and was refused twice, and has stopped trying.

personality.summary: A deadlight qi practitioner on the only body in the setting where the colony's effects and the colony's prohibitions are both measurable. She has no ceiling and no register, and her practice writes a permanent record of itself into the stone without her consent.
traits: Gives a reading on the spot and can be heard doing it, which is the whole of her value to a survey and the whole of her exposure.
Knows within the day when she has opened something, because the ground tells her before the register would.
Refuses to be entered as anything other than what she is, in writing, more than once.
Carries a lamp she does not need and cannot be talked out of.
Sits longer than anyone else on the floor, and it is not for the reason it looks like.
mannerisms: Does not move her head quickly, and is not slowed by the dark.
Sets the lamp down before working, every time, and picks it up again when somebody else needs it.
Looks at the wall rather than at the speaker, and it is a reading, not an evasion.
Counts the days aloud when she is marking a stone, and stops the moment anybody asks what the number is.
motivations: To be asked a second question by somebody who has actually heard the first.
To learn what the mind path feels like before her span closes, because it is open and she has not spent it.
To keep her practice off the wall, which she cannot do and has not stopped trying to.
flaws: Believes the markers are legible to her and is right about herself and wrong about everybody else.
Will not stop practising to keep the ground clean, which is a position she can defend and cannot afford.
Cannot accept a figure she has not measured herself, and there is almost nothing left for her to accept.
personality.voice: Level, unhurried, and unexpectedly formal, because she is used to being the reader and not the read. She answers a question twice: once in the plain words the room can use, then again in the sentence that is actually true, and she waits for the second one to be heard.
taboos: Entering a marker as anything other than a reading of her own qi.
Calling a practice done because the wall is written on.
Switching the lamp off when nobody else is on the floor.

relationships.note: The lichen colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, and a mineral bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it. That is exactly the substrate the marker grows on and exactly the difference her subspecies is named for.
A replacement symbiont in the same body plan. The difference is one mineral lattice where the hyphal colony was, and it cost two hundred and fifty years and bought back the mind path.
She is the whole of one side of that dispute, recorded on a body where both what the colony did for the parent and what it prevented can be measured against the parent.

A measurement taken by eye is provisional until someone has heard it. The survey's best instrument is the one body on the plains that can also hear, which is her, and the reading is still provisional because nobody else can cross-examine it.

A heresy is disputed over whether there is a test site, and the mind path on the mortal plains is a body with the mind path open. She is the one piece of evidence that could settle it and has been argued over rather than examined.
Neither the colony nor its replacement can survive an open sky, so a subspecies that lost its symbiont did not gain a homeland and lost the only one it had.

reference_stats.summary: She holds qi rather than spending it, so nothing in her tires and nothing in her is repaired, and there is no structural gate for her to fail and therefore no ordinal for her to quote. Her unbounded capability is real and has never once been registerable.
strengths: Refines at a rate the parent species cannot match, because a bloom holds qi where a colony transacted with it, and the discipline is slow for a body whose interior answers nothing.
Sees in the dark without a colony, which makes her the only body on a quarry floor that does not need a lamp and the only one nobody can walk up on.
Cannot be fatigued, because nothing in her is being worked and nothing is being repaired.
Carries an unmediated interior, so she is the only person alive who can report from the inside what a symbiosis does to a nervous system.
weaknesses: Nothing in this body is repaired, so a fracture is a fracture for the rest of a ninety-year life.
The bloom holds qi and cannot discharge it, so a practice that asks for a release has nothing to release into.
There is no structural gate in her to fail, which means there is no rung to name, and no register anywhere prices a discipline with no rungs.
Fragile, short-lived for her line, and cannot leave the caves for exactly the reason her parent cannot.
reference_stats.combat_read: Extraordinary and short. She does not tire and does not heal, which reads as an unbeatable body until the first real injury, after which every subsequent fight is fought with a smaller margin than the last. She is also very difficult to read, because a mineral bloom cannot discharge and nothing that enters her leaves, so a fight against her is a fight against a body that is quietly filling up. Anything that depends on her giving something up will do better than anything that depends on her running out.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is anatomical and it is the same clause the species record uses: a bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it. That single fact produces both halves. She has no ceiling, because nothing in her is constrained by a structure she lacks; and she has nothing in her being repaired, because a bloom renews nothing. What I have added is the consequence nobody had written down: a bloom is the substrate the trial-field lichen colonises, so her own practice becomes a marker in somebody else's ledger. That connection is between two authored records rather than quoted from one, and I have not stated it as a mechanical rule anywhere, because the bible does not. In terms of the yin-yang pair: her advantage is unbounded capability and her cost is that it is permanently, publicly, and involuntarily legible on a quarry wall she does not own.

identity.realm: Eleventh gate, and the wall is his parent's rather than his: a brinecaller's sac is shallower than a saltfolk's but still runs dorsal to the spine, so the vessel behind it is still split and cannot be rejoined across it. He clears the du and ren vessels separately and has never found the discipline that rejoins the pair, and he is nowhere near it — the sixth is the last place his refinement stops being something he can attribute. Every channel he opens arrives with a twin in the other chemistry, and above the sixth the pairs begin to answer each other and he cannot tell apart from pair. He stopped going to look for a rung and started going where the work is, which is not the same thing and is worth more.

appearance.presentation: Ovar Drenn stands on the bank rather than in it, weight even on two feet, with the stillness of somebody waiting for a current rather than for a customer.
appearance.age: Forty-four, old enough to have learned that the run moves and young enough to still expect the crossings to be where they were.
appearance.build: Brinecaller, the one documented crossing of the salt-adapted people with the fully watered ones. The only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced because both parents are trapped by their own element. Broad through the ribcage and long in the forearm, with the shallower sac that came with the crossing reading as a smooth back rather than the saltfolk ridge. Moves like a person who has never once needed to hurry a step in either water.
appearance.complexion: Wet-weather pale, with the knuckles permanently softened and a salt line at the collar that never quite washes out.
appearance.hair: Dark, cut to the jaw and out of fashion everywhere, because he is in transit more often than he is in a room.
appearance.eyes: Level and weather-tired, and they go to the water first in every conversation, which people read as rudeness and which is habit.
appearance.palette: Tarred rope brown, wet slate, the brass of a cut that has been read a thousand times, and a pale green at the cuffs where two different waters have dried on the same cloth.
appearance.attire: Boots that work in either medium and are proof of neither, a doubled coat, high collar, sleeves fastened, and a livery cut that opens at a gate and is worn closed everywhere else.
appearance.marks: A weal across the left shoulder from a boom he came up under and did not report, and both palms permanently creased from rope.
appearance.bearing: Composed, unhurried and permanently between two things, with a habit of checking the water before he checks the people.

canon.role_in_story: Both of his parents are trapped by their own element — one cannot leave the pan, the other cannot leave the water — and the crossing is the single biological answer to being trapped twice, and that answer is a merchant, which is why it spread. Ovar Drenn refines qi in the only body in this setting whose frame does not tell an office where it belongs, so the credential he wears is the only ground he has: passage livery exists because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person, nobody may levy a seat, and cloth is the one credential anybody can check at a boundary that is not a wall. The cost is that a thing which identifies what a traveller may open is a thing worn, not held, and every channel his discipline opens comes back with a twin he did not ask for.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a gate on the Widow Run with his livery open and a stoppered flask in each hand, weighing a barge against a standing weight and refusing to quote a figure until the water was in his mouth.
canon.lore: The run's bed moves far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it, so the useful service at any crossing on it is re-finding it rather than maintaining it, and the population that can do that is the population that can drink what is on either side of the question. He is a courier, which is the whole of his species' reason for existing, and the reason it spread: a saltfolk cannot leave the pan and a tide body cannot leave the water, and a body that metabolises both is a body that can be sent. The discipline is slower for him than for a saltfolk specialist, because the same effort is spent on osmoregulation and nothing in this body can be spared from the kidneys, and the result is that he is competent everywhere and formidable nowhere. He clears the du and ren vessels separately, one at a time, which is the saltfolk pattern inherited untouched — the crossing gave him a body that can cross and did not give him a body that can finish. The chong, which splits the penetrating vessel behind the sac at the eleventh, is his parents' wall and his is shallower but not absent. He has no intention of testing it. What makes his practice strange is not the wall but the duplication: every channel he opens arrives with a twin in the other chemistry. That is a direct consequence of being the crossing — there is no version of a brinecaller that takes one medium cleanly — and below the sixth the pairs still separate cleanly and he can work. Above it they begin to answer each other, and a pair he cannot attribute is a pair he cannot spend, and he has described this, in his own words, as being unable to tell which of them he is doing. The institutional half of his position is that he is the only body in this setting that a visitor office can actually post rather than merely tolerate. A garrison holding ground its own faction cannot staff from is staffed by visitors, and a brinecaller needs no visiting rights because neither bank is his and both feed him. So he has been posted four times and has been offered a standing term twice, and has taken one of each, and the standing term is written against a cut rather than against a name, which is the arrangement a body with no native ground can actually hold. He is not mistreated. He is postable, which is a different thing and is what a credential exists to make possible.
history: Was raised between a pan settlement and a river community, in neither of which he could claim a childhood, and learned early to be legible on paper rather than familiar.
Took a first courier term at nineteen because a body that can drink both waters is the only one a crossing can be run on, and has been on the road since.
Opened the sixth gate and stopped climbing deliberately, after working out that above it he could no longer attribute a pair, which cost him an offer and a certain amount of standing.
Was issued a passage livery and discovered that the credential, not the body, was what an office kept on file, and has worn it closed everywhere except at a gate ever since.
Took a standing term written against a cut rather than a name, which is the only form of tenure available to somebody with no native ground.

personality.summary: A brinecaller qi practitioner, competent at every gate below the sixth and unable to attribute a pair above it. He is the only body in the setting with no native ground, which makes him the only one an office can post rather than merely tolerate, and the credential on his chest is the whole of the difference between those two things.
traits: Weighs before he quotes, and will not name a figure while there is any other question outstanding.
Checks the water before he checks the people in a conversation.
Turns down a term that would tie him to a bank and accepts one written against a cut.
Reads a hull or a hull-strike the way his river notaries do, by feel and under the waterline.
Keeps two waters in two skins and chooses deliberately, which is a small daily act and the whole of his species' argument.
mannerisms: Opens his livery at a gate and closes it the instant he is through, every time.
Weighs things in his hands while other people talk.
Answers a question about belonging by asking what water the questioner drinks.
Stands on the bank rather than in it when there is no reason to be wet, which is habit and not fastidiousness.
motivations: To be posted on his own terms rather than tolerated on somebody else's.
To be credited with a practice he can describe, which no office in this setting has room for.
To drink whatever is put in front of him and be right about it.
flaws: Has no native ground and has stopped expecting to acquire any, which makes him easy to post and hard to grieve.
Refuses to climb past the sixth on the strength of arithmetic and has not tested whether he is right.
Treats the livery as a tool and is only now noticing that it is also the only document that has ever claimed him.
personality.voice: Brisk, transactional and warmer than he expects, with a contractor's habit of stating a weight before a judgement. He names his own standing last and never unprompted.
taboos: Accepting a term written against a bank.
Opening a pair above the sixth on purpose.

relationships.note: The run's bed moves far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it, so each flood recharged the sump on a schedule nobody had to decide, and the useful service at a crossing here is re-finding it rather than maintaining it.

Cloth and cut identify what a traveller is and what they may open, because a world boundary is not a wall but the edge of a law budget. The credential is the only ground he has, and it is worn rather than held.

The parent that cannot leave the pan. Its kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, and its sac runs dorsal to the spine and splits the penetrating vessel, which is the wall the crossing inherited and did not remove.

The parent that cannot leave the water. Both parents are trapped by their own element and the crossing is the single biological answer to being trapped twice, which is a merchant, which is why it spread.
Weigh, never quote, and let nobody make the first offer, because a buyer who names a figure first forfeits standing. He holds that rule as a discipline rather than a courtesy.

The mortal-tier offices that can only be filled by non-residents exist because a polity on the lowest tier is a caretaker government, and this is the one body a visitor office can actually post rather than merely tolerate.

He is postable everywhere and native nowhere.
strengths: Metabolises brine and fresh water alike, so he is the only body on the run that can work a crossing without a change of crew at either bank.
Takes charge efficiently out of either medium, which is why his refinement is slow but never interrupted.
Clears the ordinary meridians and the du and ren vessels without difficulty, because the crossing bought him mobility rather than strength.
Reads a hull, a boom or a bank the way a river notary does, by feel and under the waterline.
weaknesses: Every channel he opens arrives with a twin in the other chemistry, and above the sixth the pairs answer each other, so he cannot tell apart from pair.
The wall at the eleventh is his parents' and untouched by the crossing, because the sac is shallower and the vessel behind it is still split.
He cannot be posted above a marsh crossing on foot and cannot be assigned to a bank, because neither chemistry is the one he lives in.
The same effort spent on osmoregulation means nothing in this body can be spared to the practice.
reference_stats.combat_read: Durable and slow, with an advantage that is logistical rather than physical: he fights well in both media and on neither shore, and an opponent who knows that can refuse to be followed. Above the sixth the duplication works against him in a fight too — a channel he opens comes back paired, so a discharge he has already made can answer him from the other chemistry, and he has learned to spend in the open rather than in sequence. What he is genuinely good at is a long unhurried contest on his own ground, and he will not be driven off it.
reference_stats.notes: The pairing here is anatomical and it is a single clause in the species record: the crossing produced the only body that metabolises brine and fresh water alike. That gives him the only uninterrupted supply in the setting and it costs him the ability to attribute his own work, because a channel that takes either medium arrives with a twin in the other. The institutional half is not a rule I have invented: the passage-livery culture exists in the bible precisely because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person and clothing is the one credential that costs nothing to check. What I have added, and have said is mine rather than quoted, is the reading that a credential is the only ground a body with no native ground can hold. Nothing mechanical is asserted anywhere in this record: no technique, item or realm rejoins the pair, and the duplication is a fact about the crossing rather than about his discipline.
